text:
Maria: quick heads-up — we're scheduling a staggered regional maintenance next Tue to rotate serving nodes and apply kernel/driver updates. target window: 2026-04-07 02:00-05:00 UTC (will run region-by-region; eu-west1 then us-west1 then us-east1). expected customer-visible impact: transient connection drains and <30s cached-prefix rewarm per node, plus brief KV cache misses. no planned model changes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Jake: thanks. can we confirm the fallback behavior? if a node is drained will traffic shift automatically to healthy nodes / smaller instance types? we should make sure canary and model-variant fallback are enabled.

Anne SRE: yes — smart routing will automatically route to warm nodes in the same region. plan is rolling drain with 60s drain + 2x buffer instances per AZ. high-level runbook:

```
1) Start window on region A.
2) Mark pool PAUSE on autoscaler for pool-regionA-serving.
3) Initiate rolling drain with --grace 60s.
4) Verify traffic shift in console (per-route p50/p95).
5) Apply kernel patch, reboot nodes one at a time.
6) Validate KV cache rewarm and model latency.
7) Unpause autoscaler and monitor for 15m.
8) Move to next region.
```

I'll be primary oncall for the actual maintenance. Jake, can you be backup for region moves? @Jake please ack. Also tagging @Tina for customer comms. We will cut canary on 1 AZ first; if any >10% error increase we abort and rollback to previous config.

Tina (Comms): ack. drafting statuspage + customer note now. Posting drafts below for quick review.

Tina (Comms): STATUSPAGE DRAFT (short):

```
Title: Planned maintenance — serving node rotation (staggered regional rollout)
Start: 2026-04-07 02:00 UTC
End: 2026-04-07 05:00 UTC
Impacted services: Redwood inference serving (regional)
Details: We will perform a rolling rotation of serving nodes in eu-west1, us-west1, and us-east1 to apply kernel/driver patches. Some requests may be routed to alternate nodes resulting in transient latency spikes or brief connection resets. We do not expect sustained degradation.
Updates: Will post updates at start, after each region, and at completion.
```

Tina (Comms): CUSTOMER EMAIL DRAFT (short):

```
Subject: Planned maintenance 2026-04-07 — rolling updates to serving nodes
Hi —
We’re scheduled to perform a rolling maintenance across our serving regions on 7 April 2026 between 02:00–05:00 UTC. During this window some requests may experience very short interruptions (typically <30s) while traffic is re-routed and caches rewarm. No action is required on your side.
If you rely on pinned latency SLAs for critical paths, please let us know and we can coordinate a dedicated window.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Ops Team
```

Jake: wording looks good. can we add a short note about webhooks/retries? some customers with strict TCP timeouts might see dropped connections — suggest they have retry/backoff enabled.

Tina (Comms): good call — adding: "we recommend retry/backoff for webhooks and long-lived connections". I'll schedule customer email at T-minus 72h and update statuspage at start + region-complete posts.

Anne SRE: operational notes for on-call handoff: primary = Anne (AM), backup = Jake (PM). Handoff sequence:
- 01:45 UTC: primary pings oncall channel and confirms runbook.
- 02:00 UTC: incident-bot posts start update.
- 02:05-02:20 UTC: watch p50/p95 for route X and model Y.
- If errors >5% for >5m, escalate to incident commander and rollback.

Anne SRE: rollout cadence: region A (eu-west1) first, 60m target; region B next with 45m; region C last with 45m. total conservative window 3h to allow extra validation.

Maria: small schedule change — we've nudged the window earlier by 60 minutes to accommodate partner backup jobs. new start 2026-04-07 01:00 UTC, end 04:00 UTC. please make sure status page and customer email reflect the earlier start.

Tina (Comms): acknowledged — updating drafts and scheduling send for 72h prior to new start. will also add a short "why earlier" note referencing partner backup alignment.

Jake: confirm I’m backup for the whole window. quick checklist for my side: ensure canary policy id=canary-serve-3 is active; model-variant fallback enabled; monitoring alert thresholds set to 5% error and 20% latency jump.

Anne SRE: noted. I will attach the live checklist in the ops-runbook channel and post the step-by-step at T-15.

Maria: final: I'm going to pin the statuspage draft and the customer email in the announcements doc and schedule the send. Thanks team — please react with :thumbsup: when you’ve read and are ready for your roles.

Jake: :thumbsup:

Anne SRE: :thumbsup:

Tina (Comms): :thumbsup:
